title: Hire ShipKit — 10-Day Activation & Interview Readiness Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact People Ops playbook for a fast-moving team hire: goal is to get a new IC (usually engineer or infra-SRE) productive and shipping small-value work within 10 calendar days. It combines a hiring readiness checklist, lightweight interview/rubric cues for fast loops, and a 10-day onboarding activation timeline with comms templates. Use for hires where rapid product impact is prioritized (small pods, urgent capacity).

Scope / When to use:
- Hiring for pod-sized roles (t-shirt size: S/M).
- Candidate already has baseline experience (not new-grad).
- Team agrees to a 10-day focused ramp and a mentor-pairing.

Quick disclaimers / guardrails:
- Not for senior hires where org-level context or architecture decisions are required.
- Security-sensitive or private-deploy roles must use private-deployment security checklist (see linked artifacts).
- Must opt-in: hiring manager + mentor + people-ops coordinator sign off before day 0.

Pre-hire checklist (to close before offer accepted):
- [ ] Hiring manager confirms 2-week list of 1–2 light-impact tasks for day 3–10. (EX: small fix, infra cleanup, test addition)
- [ ] People Ops prepares offer package and first-week calendar (w/ payroll + benefits onboarding).
- [ ] Mentor assigned and introduced in Slack. Mentor = primary technical buddy for first 30 days.
- [ ] Access plan: ticket created in IT (Jira IT-XXXX) with required systems and expected delivery times.
- [ ] Minimal home-run docs linked: repo links, local dev runbook, test harness, and short product primer (<= 3 slides).

Fast interview rubric (for compressed loop hires - used when a 2-interview funnel is needed):
- Structure: 25 min take-home/code reading + 35 min system/dev task + 30 min culture problem + 10 min Q&A. Keep total <= 2 hours.
- Focus signals (what we care about):
  - Problem framing & tradeoffs (scale + safety + testability) — 30%
  - Speed & correctness of implementation / debugging instincts — 30%
  - Clear communication & pairing compatibility — 20%
  - Learning agility (how they handle unfamiliar libs/hard constraints) — 20%
- Quick scoring guide (0–3):
  - 0 = no signal / wrong approach, 1 = partial, 2 = solid with gaps, 3 = excellent + transferable patterns.
- Minimum pass: majority 2s and no 0s on critical sections. Hiring mgr can waive one lower score if references + expediency make sense.

Offer + preboarding (day -7 to day 0) checklist:
- [ ] Offer signed, HR packet sent, payroll details captured.
- [ ] Welcome email template sent with first-day agenda + Slack/Zoom links. (Template below)
- [ ] Laptop/credentials order placed (note: for private infra allow additional 48–72h).
- [ ] Small pre-boarding item: short reading (one-pager product primer) + a 15-min call opt-in with mentor.

Day 0 — first contact / admin:
- Morning: HR intro + benefits quick orientation (30m).
- 45m: Team welcome + expectations (hiring manager). Share 10-day plan and 2-week tasks.
- 1:1: Mentor pairing & access verification (git, CI, internal docs).
- Action items: confirm access, Slack channels, calendar holds for short check-ins (daily quick stand 10–15m days 1–5).

Days 1–3 — low-friction onboarding:
- Day 1: Local dev setup checklist (pair with mentor).
  - [ ] Run repo locally, run tests (identify flaky tests), open one PR template.
  - [ ] Confirm telemetry/metrics access (read key dashboards).
- Day 2: Small bug or infra chore assigned (low blast radius).
- Day 3: First small PR merged (goal). Mentor to leave review comments focusing on shipping iteratively.

Days 4–7 — shipping micro-features:
- Deliverable: ship a scoped change that addresses a measurable outcome (improve a flaky test, small latency fix, doc cleanup tied to onboarding).
- Daily 15m pairing check-ins continue.
- Hiring manager checks: quality of PRs, time-to-respond in code review, ability to run and interpret tests.

Days 8–10 — expand scope + handoff:
- Deliverable: second change or follow-up with additional test coverage or telemetry.
- Day 10: 30m readout with manager + mentor: show what shipped, blockers, and 30-day objectives.
- Collect preliminary feedback and set 30-day success signals.

30-day success signals (used for probation checkpoint):
- Contributed at least 2 merged PRs with CI passing and owner approvals.
- Can independently run local dev environment and reproduce a customer bug.
- Demonstrated timely responsiveness in async threads and PR feedback.
- Completed at least one knowledge-sharing micro-doc (1–2 pages) on a touched component.

Comms templates (copy/paste) — Welcome Slack snippet:
- "Welcome @newhire! Excited to have you. Mentor is @mentor. First-day plan is in your calendar. If you run into access issues ping #it-help or DM @people-ops. Quick intro thread: name / role / where you’re based / one thing you’re excited to work on."

Hiring manager checklist for fast hires (brief):
- [ ] Provide 2–3 small scoped tasks that map to product impact prior to offer.
- [ ] Assign mentor and block 3–4 hours/week for first 2 weeks for pairing.
- [ ] Prepare acceptance criteria for day 10 deliverable.

People Ops tips & tacit notes (Notes to self):
- Keep interview loops short; two-stage reduces candidate fatigue. If hiring for multiple seats, run one standardized exercise to enable parallel grading.
- For timezone mismatch hires, preboard with an asynchronous checklist and record a short Loom for day 0 walk-through.
- If candidate is coming from security-sensitive background (bank, healthcare), add 48h to access provisioning and early security review.

Open questions / follow-ups (placeholders):
- Who owns the 30-day micro-doc template? (suggest: eng-docs team)
- Add canned list of low-risk starter tasks per team (housekeeping for each team) — coordinate with Eng leads.

Appendix: quick interview question bank (for 30–45m system/dev session):
- Give me a recent bug you fixed: how did you triage and validate the fix? (listen for repro steps + metrics)
- Describe a time you had to make a perf vs cost tradeoff in production. What did you measure?
- Whiteboard: implement a simple rate limiter and describe failure modes (focus on edge cases + testing).

Files to attach to candidate packet (preboard):
- Minimal Product Primer (single slide), repo readme with setup, first-week calendar, mentor contact, and security NDA if required.

Document history / change log:
- 2026-01-12 created by Amina (initial draft)
- 2026-02-03 updated: clarified rubric scoring, added preboard loom suggestion

If using: reference ENG-1217 for IT access flow and HR-452 for offer template.

---
Quick check: is this compact enough? Note: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and intentionally opinionated about "ship fast" hires. If the org prefers conservative ramps, use the longer onboarding playbook instead.
